ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 23 of 27 April 2015 (establishing AML/CFT/CPF preventative measures, corporate transparency and beneficial-ownership record-keeping duties), Executive Decree No. 406 of 23 October 2015 (implementing regulations), Cabinet Decree No. 90 of 2017 (electronic Beneficial Owners Register and filing framework), Law 25 of 12 June 1995 (Private Interest Foundations regime), and the Public Registry fee and procedural regulations. The Panamanian Financial Analysis Unit (UAF) issues binding compliance rules for licensed resident agents and reporting entities.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foundation Charter (Escritura Pública de Fundación) executed before a Panamanian Notary Public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the First Circuit, Panama City, Republic of Panama
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Registration at the Public Registry of Panama (domestic perfection); Hague Apostille by the Panama Ministry of Foreign Affairs for foreign use; consular legalization only for non-Hague Convention parties

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney appointing the Resident Agent and Foundation Council members (Poder)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the grantor's country of origin (jurisdiction of residence)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille in country of issuance or Panamanian consular legalization for non-Hague countries

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial Owner Declaration (Declaración de Beneficiario Final) signed by each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed Resident Agent (Panamanian attorney) with notarized signatures
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized attestation and authenticated signature samples; filed electronically with the Public Registry UBO module

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Criminal Record Certificate / Police Clearance of each UBO, Foundation Council member and Protector
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Dirección de Investigación Judicial (DIJ) of Panama or official criminal-record authority in the person's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Panamanian consular legalization for foreign certificates

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Bank and Professional References for each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing financial institution or licensed professional in country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized letter with Hague Apostille where applicable; retained in the resident agent's AML/KYC file

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation and ongoing risk-based screening of all UBOs, Foundation Council members, Protectors and any registered beneficiaries against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK HMT Sanctions List, the Panamanian national sanctions list and the PEP register maintained by the UAF, plus adverse-media screening. Any positive PEP, sanctions or serious adverse-media match requires enhanced due diligence (EDD), approval of the compliance officer and, where appropriate, filing of a suspicious transaction report to the UAF. Continuous monitoring applies at least semi-annually and on any event-driven triggering circumstance.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá - Online Services e-Servicios, Name Search and Name Reservation Module (https://www.registro-publico.gob.pa)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The foundation name must use Latin/Roman script. Spanish is the official registry language, but foreign-language names are admitted when transliterated phonetically into Latin characters. The name may include the expressions 'Fundación de Interés Privado', 'Private Interest Foundation' or 'Foundation'. Names must be distinctive, must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered entity, and must not contravene public order or morality.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: superintendent-regulated activity terms requiring prior ministerial or Superintendency authorization
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the requested name is identical or confusingly similar to an existing registration, or contains a sensitive token, the Public Registry issues a negative name certificate specifying grounds. The applicant may either (a) apply, via e-Servicios, for a new reservation using a materially distinctive name, or (b) appeal administratively under the Administrative Procedures Law 38 of 2017: first filing a written reconsideration request (recurso de reconsideración) before the Registrar General of the Registro Público within two working days of notification, and thereafter, upon an unfavorable decision, a hierarchical appeal (recurso de apelación) before the superior authority of the Public Registry, attaching the negative certificate, trademark registration evidence, written consent of prior name holders, or other documentary proof curing the objection.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible for statutory purposes: a Private Interest Foundation must maintain its registered office at the physical professional address of its licensed Resident Agent in Panama, where service of process, official notifications and legal correspondence can be physically received. Cloud-based administrative and bookkeeping back-offices are acceptable for day-to-day commerce but cannot replace the legal registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for a low-risk IoT e-commerce retailer: estimated 10% probability of unannounced physical on-site inspection of the resident-agent premises over a five-year operating cycle, increasing to 25-35% only upon trigger events such as sanctions screening alerts, adverse media, tax-authority queries or UAF risk classification.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law No. 25 of 12 June 1995 (Private Interest Foundations), as amended by Law No. 23 of 2015 and Law No. 21 of 2017, Articles 1-39; Executive Decree No. 27 of 1996; ancillary tariff and annual franchise provisions under Law No. 51 of 2018 and Registry Tariff Resolutions.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público de Panamá), Directorate of Legal Persons (Dirección General de Personas Jurídicas), Central Headquarters, Panama City
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foundation Charter (Acta de Constitución de Fundación de Interés Privado) - an original notarized instrument subject to inscription in the Public Registry's electronic folio system (Folio Electrónico)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Panama prescribes no statutory minimum paid-in capital for a Private Interest Foundation, but Law 25 requires the initial endowment to be sufficient to fulfil the foundation's stated purposes; market practice adopts a US$10,000 endowment. The endowment is irrevocably assigned to the foundation's patrimony, may be held domestically or abroad at the Founder's discretion, and is not subject to escrow-release or capital amortization rules for registration purposes.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF THE FOUNDATION COUNCIL OF [FOUNDATION NAME]. Adopted by unanimous written consent of the Founder and the Foundation Council on this 15th day of [MONTH, YEAR]. WHEREAS the Foundation was organized as a private interest foundation under Law 25 of 1995 and inscribed in the Public Registry of Panama; BE IT RESOLVED: (1) The US$10,000 initial endowment is subscribed and irrevocably transferred to the Foundation's patrimony for its smart home IoT hardware retail purposes; (2) The registered office is fixed at [PANAMA CITY, CALLE 50 ADDRESS] to receive judicial and administrative notices; (3) The President and Secretary-Treasurer appointments are ratified; (4) The licensed Resident Agent, [RA FIRM NAME], is confirmed as statutory service-of-process representative.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Name Clearance and Notarize the Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Name Search Section) and Notary Public of the Circuit of Panama (Primera Notaría del Circuito de Panamá)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a name-search request through the Public Registry's legal persons portal and obtain the Certificate of No Prior Registration (Certificado de No Inscripción del Nombre). Instruct a Panamanian notary to prepare the Foundation Charter in Spanish, stipulating the foundation name, registered office in Panama, initial endowment, purposes (retail distribution of smart home IoT hardware and home automation devices), Foundation Council members, optional Protector, beneficiary provisions, and the licensed Resident Agent. The Founder and all initial Council members must execute the instrument personally or by power of attorney before the notary.
required_dossiers: Name search approval certificate (Certificado de No Inscripción del Nombre)
Draft Foundation Charter in Spanish
Passports or identity documents of Founder, Council members, and officers
Protector appointment letter (if any)
Resident Agent acceptance letter with license (idoneidad) details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity or public-order conflict, the notary prepares a corrected Charter with the next available approved name and re-executes it; a minor resubmission fee (approx. US$25) applies and a fresh name certificate is issued within 24 hours.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Settle Registry Tariffs, Stamp Taxes, and the First Annual Franchise Contribution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Treasury Office / Tesorería) and authorized collection banks (Banco Nacional de Panamá, Caja de Ahorros) via the SICOM e-payment platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Calculate the inscription tax by applying the Registry tariff table to the declared endowment (customary US$10,000). Pay the notarial protocol stamp tax, the Public Registry inscription tax, and the foundation's first annual franchise contribution if billed at registration. Obtain the official electronic payment receipt (boleta única de pago) from the SICOM platform for attachment to the filing package.
required_dossiers: Notarized Foundation Charter original
Registry tariff calculation worksheet
Electronic payment receipts (boletas de pago)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry re-calculates the fee upward, pay the incremental amount at the Registry cashier within five business days; the SICOM payment status is updated electronically and the filing queue is not affected.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit the Charter Package for Inscription at the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama - Legal Persons Unit (Sección de Personas Jurídicas), Central Headquarters, Panama City (in-person or through certified courier filing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deliver the complete inscription package comprising the notarized Charter, the Resident Agent acceptance, the officers' data sheet, and the stamped proof of fee payment. The Registry clerk processes the instrument, creates the Folio Electrónico, and issues the Certificate of Registration and Legal Personality (Certificado de Personería Jurídica) after the legal review. The certificate is executed with the Registry's digital signature and serves as conclusive evidence of the foundation's existence.
required_dossiers: Original notarized Foundation Charter
Resident Agent acceptance form (formulario RA-2)
Payment receipts (boletas única)
Identity dossier of Foundation Council members
Cover letter from the formation law firm
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a reparo (formal query), the formation counsel corrects the deficient annex or clause and refiles within 30 calendar days; if the query pertains to the name, an alternative approved name is substituted via notarial protocol and refiled. Registration objections do not invalidate earlier fee payments.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Legalize Corporate Books and Obtain the Legal Entity Seal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama - Book Legalization Division (Legalización de Libros) and the Legal Persons seal office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of inscription, present three bound books in Spanish - the accounting ledger (Libro Mayor), daily journal (Libro Diario), and minutes book (Libro de Actas) - for legalization. The Registry assigns sequential folio numbers, stamps each page, and affixes the seal. Simultaneously, request the legal entity seal (sello de la persona jurídica) used for issuing certificates and executing commercial documents.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registration and Legal Personality (clean copy)
Three bound books prepared to Registry physical format
Book legalization application form
Proof of good standing if the annual franchise fee is due
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If books are rejected for margin, binding, or foliation irregularities, correct the physical format to the Registry's book guidelines and resubmit; no duplicate notarization fee is charged for the same book if prior foliation had not been recorded.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the Foundation with DGI and Obtain the RUC (Tax) Identification Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF) - RUC Digital portal and in-person taxpayer service offices in Panama City
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) application under Panama's territorial taxation regime, selecting the taxpayer activity as ISIC 4791 'Retail sale of electronic and computer equipment and peripherals, including smart home IoT devices.' Submit the founding documentation and the commercial premises data. Upon approval, the DGI assigns the 16-digit RUC and authorizes the fiscal invoicing code (Código de Facturación) used for monthly F-15 declarations for income tax (ISR) and movable goods tax (ITBM).
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registration and Legal Personality
Registry folio of the Charter and officer appointments
Passports or identity documents of the Council officers and Resident Agent
Proof of the Panama City commercial premise address (lease or counsel's letter)
Sworn declaration of economic domicile
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGI issues a requerimiento for an activity-code or domicile inconsistency, file a corrective RUC addendum (enmienda de datos) via the virtual portal; the corrected RUC is typically validated within two business days, during which the taxpayer may operate under a provisional RUC.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Verify Good Standing and Ratify the Governance Record with the Resident Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Good Standing / Paz y Salvo service) and the licensed Resident Agent under Law 32 of 2014
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm that the foundation has no pending annual franchise tax (tasa única of US$350 for private interest foundations) and obtain the Registry-issued Certificate of Good Standing (Certificado de Buena Conducta). Ensure the Resident Agent maintains at the registered office the certified copy of the Foundation Charter, the current Council appointments, and the legalized minutes book containing an organizational ratification minute. This governance package constitutes the standard due-diligence dossier for bank account opening and commercial contracting.
required_dossiers: Folio Electrónico inscription record
Payment receipts for annual franchise (tasa única) installments
Resident Agent license copy and acceptance record
Legalized minutes book with organizational ratification minutes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If good standing is withheld for unpaid annual franchise tax, pay the US$350 obligation through the Registry's SICOM e-payment and request immediate reissuance of the paz y salvo; the Registry issues the certificate the next business day after confirmation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipality of Panama (Alcaldía de Panamá) - Directorate of Commercial Licenses (Dirección de Licencias Comerciales); with supplementary industrial-environment oversight by the Ministry of the Environment (Ministerio de Ambiente - MiAMBIENTE)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Commercial Operating License and Notice of Operation (Aviso de Operación / Licencia Comercial Anual del Municipio de Panamá) - applicable to ISIC 4791 low-risk retail trade in smart home IoT hardware; no separate sectoral manufacturing license is required because the business is exclusively a retailer/distributor and does not undertake regulated production.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of the Environment of Panama (Ministerio de Ambiente - MiAMBIENTE), National Directorate of Environmental Impact Assessment (Dirección Nacional de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I - Environmental Registration (Registro Ambiental / Diagnóstico Ambiental) for low-impact commercial activities; the operation of a leased retail unit for smart home IoT hardware does not trigger a Full EIA Report or Preliminary Environmental Study under the Unified Environmental Assessment Regulation applicable to retail-commercial premises.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Sanitary sewage only to municipal collectors under MINSA Decree No. 116 of 1973 (pH 6-9, BOD5 300 mg/L domestic-strength); no process or VOC emission sources since products are sold in sealed packaging - any incidental HVAC refrigerant work follows Law No. 11 of 1992 (Montreal Protocol) with restricted ozone-depleting refrigerants; e-waste, spent lithium batteries, and consumer returns must be transferred to MiAMBIENTE-registered electronic-waste collection operators, with weigh tickets and transfer manifests retained for three years; packaging residuals must comply with municipal solid-waste sorting and recycling requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: SINAPROC (Sistema Nacional de Protección Civil) Fire-Safety Clearance Certificate (Certificado de Inspección Contra Incendios) required before opening to the public; Municipality of Panama zoning and structural-occupancy certificate for the retail premises (uso de suelo and occupancy ratings for commercial loading); workplace safety compliance under the Panamanian Occupational Safety and Health Regulation (Executive Decree No. 306 of 2006) enforced by MITRADEL and MINSA, covering electrical low-voltage inspections, storage rack structural load, means of egress, and first-aid provisions; final municipal inspection must be passed before issuance of the annual operating license.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF) — national tax authority administering the RUC (taxpayer identification), income tax (ISR) and ITBMS (VAT), accessed through the Sistema de Información Fiscal (SIF) online portal at https://sif.mef.gob.pa; export goods control: Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA); local municipal operating license: Alcaldía (Aviso de Operación). Panama has only one national tax level (no sub-national income/VAT).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the PA_PIF (Panama Private Interest Foundation under Law 25 of 1995): (1) Notarize and register the foundation charter with the Registro Público de Panamá, with initial endowment of at least USD/B/. 10,000 and a Panamanian resident agent; (2) obtain foundation council minutes appointing officers and a Panama domicile certificate; (3) file the DGI taxpayer-registration form (Solicitud de Registro de Contribuyente) at the SIF portal or an authorized DGI office, attaching an apostilled charter, certified Spanish translation if original is not Spanish, resident-agent acceptance, and proof of premises; (4) obtain the RUC number and activation certificates for ISR, ITBMS and e-invoicing modules; (5) if the PIF trades in goods, register as importer/exporter with ANA and obtain the electronic signature (Firma Electrónica) using a Panamanian ID/passport for e-invoicing; (6) if no Panama-source commercial activity exists, registration is elective, but ISIC 4791 e-commerce activity with Panamanian buyers or imports makes RUC registration mandatory.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No IRS-style check-the-box regime exists in Panama, but the following elections/classifications are available: (i) simplified ITBMS small-taxpayer election for gross annual turnover not exceeding B/. 300,000, replacing general ITBMS credit procedures with a 7% flat invoice supplement; (ii) small-retailer presumptive income-tax method for qualifying merchants, substituting the 25% standard corporate rate; (iii) territorial-source structural election: the PIF may keep all foreign-source e-commerce profits accumulated and unrepatriated as dividends, avoiding 25% ISR (only a 4% dividend/gratuity tax applies on actual distributions of foreign-source profits); (iv) Multinational HQ (SEM) elective regime — under Law 41 of 2007, a licensed SEM may claim a 5% rate on export services and ITBMS exemption, relevant only if the foundation adds cross-border B2B services; (v) practical PE election for online retail: if the PIF has no fixed place of business or dependent agent in Panama, its sales to foreign customers are treated as foreign-source and outside Panama's ITBMS/ISR net, so the foundation may elect to operate as a non-domiciled exporter, importing goods under customs ITBMS suspension with subsequent export credit.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS — Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (Panama value-added tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: B/. 300,000 of gross annual taxable turnover (Balboa at parity with USD); however, registration as an ITBMS taxpayer is mandatory from the first import of IoT hardware or from the first Panama-source retail sale if the foundation maintains a fixed establishment. The 10% ITBMS rate applies to professional services, restaurants and similar service segments, while the 7% goods rate governs ISIC 4791 hardware retail.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time DGI-authorized e-invoicing (Factura Electrónica) is phased in by taxpayer category under Law 6 of 2018 and DGI technical standards through the SIF platform. The PIF retailer must: (a) obtain an 8/12-digit DGI Código de Autorización for each invoice in near-real time, either through the DGI REST/API gateway or DGI web forms; (b) transmit the invoice XML in the DGI schema and store the signed digital objects for audit; (c) print/show the authorization code and DGI fiscal legend on every Panamanian customer receipt; (d) integrate Stripe and Shopify Payments with a DGI-certified local e-invoicing adjunct or ERP API so each Panama-sourced sale is declared in the monthly ITBMS return; (e) adopt electronic sales/purchase books in SIF; (f) flag export transactions with the 'exportacion' reason to evidence 0% rates and support input-credit claims. Failure to transmit triggers rejection of input credits and administrative fines.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: ITBMS zero-rating (0%) is available where: (i) tangible IoT hardware is physically exported from Panama under a definitive customs export declaration, with ownership transferred and goods delivered outside Panama; (ii) the buyer of record is not a resident of Panama and the sale is settled from abroad; (iii) digital IoT software/firmware is delivered electronically to customers using the services outside Panama; or (iv) services are provided to a foreign counterparty without Panamanian use. DGI examines the cumulative file: real export declaration, pecuniary settlement evidence, and the PIF's accounting trail. Panama has no exchange-control repatriation deadline because the USD is the circulating currency, but the inward-remittance certificate and/or the Stripe/Shopify settlement ledger mapping to each export invoice is the substantive evidence required; free-trade-zone and maquila modalities benefit from ITBMS suspension with 0% on the re-export.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Panama Customs DUA export declaration (Salida Definitiva) or Free-Zone transfer document, with ANA validation stamp
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or international courier/postal export receipt proving physical cross-border delivery
Commercial invoice and packing list matching the DUA and payment evidence
Inward Remittance Certificate (boleta de remesa) or equivalent bank statement/Stripe-Shopify settlement ledger evidencing receipt from abroad
E-invoice with DGI authorization code showing ITBMS 0% and the export reason code
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI, ANA and the banking system cross-match export declarations with paid ITBMS returns, customs departure data and banking inflows. Where zero-rating is improperly claimed: (1) the 7% ITBMS on the full gross amount is assessed retroactively together with a 10% surcharge and 1% monthly interest; (2) fiscal-code penalties of 50%-200% of the evaded tax apply for proven fraud; (3) refunded input credits are clawed back with interest for up to five years of statute of limitations; (4) criminal tax evasion (Law 8 of 2010 and Law 76 of 2019) is punishable with 2-5 years imprisonment and fines; (5) customs violations expose the PIF to fines of up to 300% of goods value, cancellation of the exporter license, and debarment from ANA authorized-operators programs; (6) foundation council members and the resident agent may face solidary liability for fraudulent export returns.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama does not operate a central bank. The Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) is the sole banking and AML/CFT supervisory authority. Banco Nacional de Panamá (BNP) acts as fiscal agent for the Treasury but has no monetary policy power. Monetary conditions are set de facto by the U.S. Federal Reserve as a result of full dollarization.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The U.S. dollar is unlimited legal tender under Executive Decree No. 154 of 1904, complemented by Law 84 of 1941; the balboa is a purely nominal accounting unit and no balboa paper currency is issued. Panama therefore has absolute convertibility on both current and capital account items. There are no profit repatriation restrictions, no capital controls, and no prior approval requirements for inbound or outbound transfers. For an offshore Private Interest Foundation conducting cross-border IoT retail, funds generated from foreign sales are considered territory-exclusive income and can be freely remitted to bank accounts worldwide. Compliance obligations derive solely from SBP AML rules (Law 23 of 2015) and require documentation of the underlying trade or capital contribution, not FX authorization.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Panama imposes no statutory timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no surrender requirement for export proceeds. The foundation may retain 100% of proceeds in USD, CNH, EUR, or any freely convertible currency in domestic or foreign accounts. For internal underwriting, the foundation should retain export invoices, bills of lading (AWB/SEAWAY), and marketplace payout reports to evidence the commercial provenance of inbound funds and mitigate any bank's perception of unexplained wealth.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational USD/EUR Account; optional segregated Capital Escrow Account for the endowed base capital of the Private Interest Foundation
Operational USD Account with merchant settlement sub-ledgers for Stripe/Shopify payouts and trade disbursements; private banking desk for non-resident foundation councils
Operational USD Account with Documentary Import Letter of Credit (SWIFT MT700) facility
Operational USD Account for e-commerce receivables and supplier payments

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderate-Low. Panama enacted the Financial Innovation Regime (regulatory sandbox) under Law 70 of 2022 and the SBP regulates licensed fintech payment/electronic-money participants; however, no foreign offshore EMI (e.g., Airwallex, Currenxie, Wise Business) holds a Panamanian payment-services or e-money license in good standing. Such EMIs may be used as auxiliary collection or disbursement tools for HKD/CNH and EUR payments to Chinese or European suppliers, but the foundation's primary liquidity anchor must be a licensed Panamanian bank account. Major domestic banks frequently reject inbound wires from third-party pooled settlement accounts of EMIs absent a clean beneficiary-owner name, an EMI bank reference, and a breakdown of each merchant payout. The recommended architecture is to use the EMI for supplier-side disbursements and to sweep all net merchant proceeds monthly via SWIFT MT103 into the Panamanian bank account, attaching Stripe/Shopify reconciliation reports.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under Law 23 of 2015 and SBP CDD standards, face-to-face identity verification is the default expectation for non-resident foundation council members and protectors. An in-person interview at the bank's Panama City office is the strongest application posture and materially accelerates account opening. Remote onboarding is possible on a case-by-case basis only at private-banking desks (e.g., Towerbank) using simultaneous video verification, apostilled and consul-legalized passports, notarized signatures before a notary public in the resident country, the registered copy of the Foundation Deed, and a closing legal opinion issued by a licensed Panamanian law firm. In all cases the original Foundation Deed and Registry Certificate (Copia Literal) must be physically filed with the bank; at least one member of the Foundation Council is normally required to appear personally to execute the account mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk structure inference: a Panamanian Private Interest Foundation with unregistered bearer beneficiary rights is perceived as a potential concealment vehicle for non-resident families (asset protection or tax evasion)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the registered Foundation Deed from the Registro Público de Panamá; Certificate of Good Standing; Foundation Council resolution appointing signatories; a written Beneficial Ownership Declaration executed by the council identifying all beneficiaries and their risk profiles; sworn source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements from the founder; and a structure chart signed by the licensed Registered Agent demonstrating no bearer instruments are outstanding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Merchant-aggregator risk: Stripe and Shopify Payments receive card payments across multiple countries and are treated by banks as high-velocity electronic-money channels that may conceal sub-merchant traffic, sanctions exposure, or undisclosed third-party settlements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed Stripe and Shopify merchant agreements naming the foundation as legal merchant; monthly payout reports reconciled to settlement amounts; PCI-DSS Attestation of Compliance for the IoT store; a list of active selling platforms and product stock-keeping units (SKUs); and a sworn declaration that no third-party payment aggregation or pass-through of funds occurs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Jurisdictional mismatch: the foundation is a Panamanian legal entity but payment traffic originates from U.S./EU/ASEAN consumers and may be interpreted as an unlicensed payment business
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Panamanian legal opinion clarifying that the foundation is a commercial goods retailer and not an electronic money institution or money remitter; sale-and-purchase contracts demonstrating title transfer of IoT hardware to customers; customs/export documentation for goods shipped from fulfillment centers in Hong Kong/Shenzhen/Miami; and platform confirmation that Stripe and Shopify are the regulated payment processors of record.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of economic substance: minimal physical footprint in Panama may trigger 'shell entity' red flags and denial of domiciliation benefits
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered office lease contract in Panama; utility and property maintenance records; annual minutes of the Foundation Council kept at the registered office; an updated payroll register if any local representative is hired; and an operational or logistics services agreement with a Panama-based fulfillment or customs brokerage firm to evidence real activity where economically warranted.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For the founder's capital injection, route a SWIFT MT103 from the founding family's own bank account to the foundation's Panama account with the beneficiary reference 'Contribution to Capital of PIF No. XX'; the transaction should be free of any goods description and supported by a Foundation Council capitalization resolution. For e-commerce settlement, use Stripe's payout engine to send USD to the Panama account via Stripe's U.S. or European banking partners (typically routed through Citibank/JPMorgan New York), and for smaller balances use Wise Business 'Business Multi-currency' only as a collection acceleration tool. Panama imposes no statutory purpose code, but best practice is to include descriptive remittance information such as 'FOUNDATION CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION', 'MERCHANT SETTLEMENT - STRIPE PAYOUTS', or 'REIMBURSEMENT OF TRADE ADVANCE' and attach the original payout report to the bank on request. All inbound wires from aggregators should arrive with the foundation as named beneficiary, never in the name of an individual council member, and should be matched to monthly payroll/settlement statements within 3 business days to satisfy the SBP's transaction monitoring expectations.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rail for supplier settlements is the SWIFT MT103 with fee division field SHA (charges shared) to prevent correspondent deductions from eroding the supplier's net payment. For regular procurement of smart IoT hardware from Shenzhen or Hong Kong manufacturers under USD 50,000 per invoice, use direct telegraphic transfer with attached purchase order. For consolidated bulk shipments exceeding USD 100,000, open an irrevocable documentary Letter of Credit (SWIFT MT700 issued by Banco General, Banistmo, or Multibank) with a 90-day usance tenor, payable at sight against bills of lading and commercial invoice. Alternative rails include trade financing facilities (import loans or trust receipts secured by the LC) and HKD/CNH disbursements via licensed EMIs for urgent top-up of supplier accounts. All cross-border payments must flow from the operational account only, with six-month settlement history and underlying trade invoices maintained and electronically retrievable for the bank's post-transaction compliance reviews.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/CNH deliverable forward contracts (1M to 12M) transacted at the dealing desks of Banco General or Banistmo for settling Chinese suppliers without converting core USD liquidity
CNY non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) entered into with U.S. or Hong Kong counterparties when the foundation has no onshore CNY bank account, based on standard international NDF documentation
USD/EUR FX swaps and rolling forward contracts to hedge European wholesale purchases and to convert EUR balances generated by Shopify Markets
USD/EUR cross-currency swaps for term-aligned hedging of supplier credit lines, subject to ISDA and CSTA master agreements executed with a licensed bank dealer
Plain-vanilla USD/CAD and USD/MXN forward contracts to hedge Canadian and Mexican retail payout repatriation if multi-currency collection accounts are later adopted

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Maintenance Franchise Tax for Private Interest Foundation (Tasa Administrativa Anual)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually between January 1 and June 30; due on or before June 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment surcharge of 10% of the tax plus monthly statutory interest; non-payment for two consecutive years triggers administrative dissolution by the Public Registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial-Owner Sworn Declaration (LAW 70 of 2019 – Beneficial Owner Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Beneficial Owner Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before June 30; any change in beneficial ownership must be updated within 30 calendar days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly administrative fine up to US$1,000; suspension of access to public registry certificates and legal/tax proceedings until regularization.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return (Declaración Jurada de Renta) – required only if the foundation generates Panama-source taxable income
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 15 following the calendar tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Surcharge of 5%–10% of the tax due plus monthly default interest at the Panamanian statutory rate; persistent non-compliance may result in criminal tax proceedings and prohibition of commercial activities.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Panama Private Interest Foundation is exempt from statutory audit unless it conducts commercial activities in Panama and exceeds Executive Decree No. 103 of 2003 thresholds: annual gross revenue over US$1.5 million or total assets over US$3.0 million.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for entities required to present audited financial statements; IFRS for SMEs is acceptable for the internal statutory books of a non-publicly traded Private Interest Foundation.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The registered agent must obtain an annual certified confirmation from the Foundation Council disclosing the settlor, council members, protector (if any) and all beneficial owners. Under Law 70 of 2019 the sworn declaration must be filed with the DGI by June 30 each year. Any transfer of foundation interests is recorded internally in the interests register; no public amendment is filed with the Public Registry.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$2,500 – US$8,000 (if audit triggered; otherwise US$0)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% on net taxable income derived from Panamanian-source revenue (Código Fiscal Art. 699; small taxpayers under Law 84 of 2017 may benefit from a 15%–25% progressive bracket scale).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial tax system: only Panamanian-source income is taxed; foreign-source revenue of a Private Interest Foundation (PIF) registered under Law 25 of 1995, including global IoT hardware sales through Stripe/Shopify settled abroad, is outside the Panamanian tax base. No CFC or worldwide aggregation rules apply to foreign passive income; capital gains on foreign assets are exempt; no gross receipts tax on exports; PIF distributions to beneficiaries sourced from foreign assets are not subject to Panamanian income tax; PIFs pay a fixed annual foundation franchise fee rather than an income tax on offshore endowments.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 745 (Declaración Jurada de Impuesto Sobre la Renta – Personas Jurídicas) filed electronically through the DGI e-Tax 2.0 portal (https://etax.dgi.gob.pa). Ancillary annexes include Form 745-Anexo for exemptions, the Transfer Pricing Affidavit, and quarterly advance payment returns (Anticipos).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return, plus quarterly advance income tax payments (anticipos).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return must be filed within three months following the fiscal year-end; a calendar-year PIF must file on or before 31 March of the succeeding year. Quarterly anticipos are due in the month following each quarter based on the prior year's tax liability.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Ingresos brutos gravables de fuente panameña (gross taxable income from Panamanian source).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only retail revenue physically sourced in Panama (e.g., delivered/fulfilled to Panamanian addresses). Exclude Stripe/Shopify settlements attributable to foreign customers where inventory, contracts, and fulfillment occur abroad, and retain geolocation, shipping, and gateway records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Costos y gastos deducibles relacionados con ingresos gravables (deductible expenses and costs).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate only expenses traceable to Panamanian-source sales (COGS, platform commission, freight, tariffs, local marketing). Keep contemporaneous documentation for e-commerce platform fees and intercompany recharges.
Net taxable amount after permitted deductions; a PIF with zero Panamanian-source revenue will show zero in this box and should attach a territorial-source memorandum.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Impuesto calculado a la tarifa del 25% (computed income tax).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply 25% only if Línea 3 is positive; otherwise enter zero. No shadow worldwide basis is used unless the DGI fiscal transparency trigger rules apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Anticipos pagados, créditos y retenciones (advance payments, credits, and withholdings).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credit all quarterly anticipos paid and any Panamanian WHT certificates issued by local payment processors; retain e-Tax payment receipts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Saldo a pagar o saldo a favor (net tax payable or refund).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Final treasury position. A PIF claiming a refund of anticipos must attach a territorial-source certification and foreign bank settlement evidence.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing and late payment attract a 1% monthly surcharge (capped at 60% of the tax due) plus statutory late interest; administrative fines range from B/.100 to B/.5,000 under Código Fiscal Art. 712; failure to remit advance payments triggers 25% aggravating surcharge in tax audits; wilful non-filing or false filing is prosecuted criminally (2–5 years imprisonment under Arts. 758–761). Penalties survive the voluntary dissolution of a PIF.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 5% final dividend withholding on distributions paid from Panamanian-taxed profits (Código Fiscal Art. 733); 10% withholding applies to distributions from non-taxed or fiscally transparent profits. A PIF distributing foreign-sourced foundation assets or foreign-derived income to beneficiaries is not subject to Panamanian dividend WHT by reason of territoriality; however, Panamanian-source commercial profits distributed through a PIF are subject to the 5% dividend tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama applies DTAs (e.g., with Korea, Mexico, Singapore, Spain, France, Portugal, UAE) and TIEA frameworks through a source-withholding or refund mechanism. Protocol: (1) obtain the beneficiary's Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) from its home tax authority, apostilled or legalized as required; (2) complete the DGI e-Tax 2.0 'Aplicación de Convenios' module or file the standard withholding-relief annex with the withholding agent before payment; (3) submit TRC, audited financials showing beneficial ownership, and transactional documentation proving no abusive conduit; (4) obtain case-specific DGI authorization to apply the treaty-reduced rate (typically 5%–0% dividends); (5) if the reduced rate is applied at source erroneously, the excess may be recovered through a refund adjustment on Form 745. Processing typically takes 60–180 days.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties for use of trademarks, patents, software, and IoT IP paid from Panamanian source: 12.5% statutory WHT on gross amount (Código Fiscal Art. 734); treaty rates commonly reduce to 10% or 5%. Interest paid to non-resident lenders on cross-border finance: 6% statutory final WHT (Art. 733), with 0% available where the interest qualifies under registered international loan exemptions; DTAs may reduce or exempt interest. Failure to withhold exposes the PIF to 100% surcharge on the withheld amount plus monthly interest.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File and annual TP Affidavit are mandatory in Balboas (B/., pegged 1:1 to USD) where the PIF's related-party transactions exceed B/. 350,000 in a fiscal year; Master File is required when the consolidated multinational group to which the PIF belongs reports prior-year gross revenue equal to or above B/. 50,000,000. Depending on DGI implementing resolutions, taxpayers with gross revenue above B/. 3,000,000 and intercompany goods or services may also be documented regardless of the 350k threshold.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Other acceptable method when the above are not the most appropriate (Art. 778-E Código Fiscal)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama does not apply an offshore ESR statute of the BVI/UAE type, but the following substance rules bind a PIF: (1) the territorial exemption is available only if the IoT retail business is genuinely managed and executed abroad—Panama-point contacts, Panamanian fulfilment centers, or local managers can convert income into Panamanian source; (2) under the fiscal transparency trigger doctrine (Law 52 of 2016 and DGI rulings), a PIF whose Panamanian-source income falls below 50% of total global gross income may be forced to include foreign income in the taxable base unless it proves real economic activity, local registered office, Foundation Council minutes, local books, payroll, and decision-making records; (3) DGI audits require a logical substance file: foundation charter, council resolutions approving each commercial venture, distribution of e-commerce commissions, and bank statements. Absence of substance is treated as misuse of the PIF form, generating ex-officio assessments and 25% surcharges.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately booking worldwide IoT retail revenue as foreign-source when the PIF maintains a Panamanian stock warehouse, employs local support staff, or transacts with Panamanian consumers via a Panamanian merchant account; falsifying Form 745 to zero; failing to declare Panamanian-source e-commerce income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal defraudación tributaria under Código Fiscal Arts. 758–761: fines ranging from 100% to 300% of the evaded tax and imprisonment from 2 to 5 years; civil reassessment including worldwide income retroactively, 1% monthly surcharge (capped at 60%), and nullification of tax-exemption certificates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foundation Council members who sign false returns are jointly and severally liable for the tax debt and penalties; courts may order civil restitution to the foundation and beneficiaries, freeze personal assets, impose preventive travel bans (prohibición de salida del país), and sentence directors to imprisonment for fraudulent declarations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the PIF as a mere title-holding shell with no local registered-office presence, no Foundation Council meetings, no accounting records, and no commercial rationale while claiming Panama-source retail income exemption or treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI re-characterization of the foundation as a taxable commercial entity, inclusion of foreign income under the fiscal transparency rule, 25% tax on the global base, surcharges of up to 60%, administrative fines up to B/.5,000, and denial of the PIF's statutory incompatibilities; the registry may cancel the foundation's inscription for manifest non-activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under Law 25 of 1995, Council members acting ultra vires or with gross negligence are personally liable for damages; in tax proceedings the corporate veil is pierced where the foundation is a mere alter ego—directors face personal assessments for the full reassessed liability, bankruptcy-restriction orders, and defensive custody while criminal tax charges are pending.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Law 23 of 2015 Breach with Payment Rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the IoT retail business through Stripe/Shopify Payments without registering as a non-financial obliged subject (sujeto obligado no financiero), failing to conduct KYC/KYB on high-risk resellers, accepting third-party card settlements, or failing to report suspicious transactions to the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) in respect of crypto or high-volume cross-border payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Monetary fines of up to B/.1,000,000 for repeat or serious AML violations by non-financial subjects; violation of suspicious transaction reporting rules triggers administrative disqualification and criminal money-laundering charges under Law 23 of 2015, punishable by 5 to 12 years of imprisonment for predicate offences involving illicit funds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foundation Council members and compliance officers are criminally liable where they knowingly permit laundering through the retail pay in-flow; sanctions include personal fines, forfeiture of personal assets, travel restrictions, extradition exposure under AML treaties, and imprisonment of 5–12 years; directors are also subject to permanent debarment from founding or managing Panamanian legal entities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Engaging in intercompany procurement of IoT hardware, software licensing, allocation of overhead, or financing with related parties above the B/. 350,000 threshold without preparing Local File, Master File, or the annual TP Affidavit, or applying a non-arm's length margin that shifts profit from Panamanian retail distribution to a foreign affiliate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI may adjust the taxable base to the arm's length result and impose the 25% corporate tax on the upward adjustment, plus 1% monthly default surcharges and late interest; failure to submit TP documentation attracts administrative fines of B/. 1,000 to B/. 10,000 per infraction and increases the burden of proof to the taxpayer; repeat violations permit aggregate penalties of up to B/. 50,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false TP affidavits face criminal liability for false statements (1–4 years imprisonment); civil liability extends to the entire TP adjustment where the Council approved artificial margins without economic justification, including restitution to the foundation and disgorgement of commissions; judges may impose personal preventive detention in aggravated fraud-linked TP audits.
